author: PavelMakarchuk
body:
Three things flagged here, taking each in turn:

**On "PE doesn't show tax before credits"**: re-running this case against current PE (1.691.3), the output's `Tax before credits` line shows **$5,422**, not $0 — MT tax on $100,482 taxable income (4.7% × $21,100 + 5.9% × $79,381). Stress-tested at $1M of wages → $56,635 of MT tax, so the "no tax on incomes >$1M" pattern doesn't reproduce in current PE.

**On v32 = $0 in the output**: this is a PE-taxsim emulator display bug — fix in [#901](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-taxsim/pull/901). The `taxsim_v32_state_agi` adapter reads PE-US's unified `state_agi` variable, which sums `gov.states.household.state_agis`. That list points to [`mt_agi_indiv`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/main/policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/mt/tax/income/base/mt_agi_indiv.py) (a person-level variable `defined_for` MFS-on-same-return only) — so for joint/single/HoH MT filers it returns $0. The MT tax computation itself reads [`mt_agi_joint`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/main/policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/mt/tax/income/base/mt_agi_joint.py) and is correct; only the v32 row was wrong. The PR adds an override routing v32 to `mt_agi_joint` for MT.

**On the $10K Schedule I addback**: PE doesn't add back $10K here, which matches your reading. Per the [2025 MT Form 2 Schedule I](http://taxsim.nber.org/out2psl/862/), Part I line 4 is "State income tax deduction included in federal taxable income." This filer's federal itemized deductions are property tax + mortgage interest only — no state income tax — so PE correctly returns $0 in additions, giving MT taxable income = $100,482. TaxAct's PDF shows +$10K → $110,482, which we don't see a basis for unless TaxAct is using a stale pre-OBBBA SALT-cap-leftover rule. PE looks correct on the law here.
